1: Lists of names from Adam through Noah's sons to Abraham, and the families of Ishmael and Esau.
Israel's story is placed inside the story of the whole human race.
2: The sons of Israel, then the family of Judah down to Jesse and David.
The writer goes first to the royal tribe.
3: David's sons, the kings of Judah after Solomon, and the royal family after the exile.
David's line continued even when there was no throne.
4: More clans of Judah and of Simeon. Jabez prays that God will bless him and keep him from harm, and God grants it.
A short prayer hidden in a list shows that God hears individuals.
5: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. They win battles when they cry to God, and are later exiled for their idolatry.
Trust brings help; unfaithfulness brings loss.
6: The line of the high priests, the Temple singers appointed by David, and the Levites' towns.
Worship has an ordered ministry handed down through generations.
7: Family lists of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher.
Every tribe is remembered as part of Israel.
8: The clans of Benjamin, ending with the family of King Saul and Jonathan.
The first king's family is recorded before his story is told.
9: The people, priests, Levites and gatekeepers who settled again in Jerusalem after the exile.
The lists show the returned exiles that they belong to the same people.
10: Saul and his sons die fighting the Philistines on Mount Gilboa.
The writer's verdict: Saul died for his unfaithfulness and for consulting a medium.
11: All Israel anoints David at Hebron. He takes Jerusalem. His mighty men and their exploits are listed.
David's kingdom rests on God's word and on loyal friends.
12: Warriors from every tribe come over to David, even while he is still a fugitive.
Unity gathers around the king God has chosen.
13: David sets out to bring the ark to Jerusalem on a cart. Uzzah steadies it with his hand and dies. The ark stays three months with Obed-edom.
Good intentions do not replace doing things God's way.
14: Hiram sends cedar for David's house. David asks God before each battle and twice defeats the Philistines.
David succeeds because he asks first.
15: This time Levites carry the ark on their shoulders as the law requires, with singers and instruments. David dances.
16: The ark is placed in its tent. David appoints Levites to praise God continually and gives them a song: "Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good."
Daily praise becomes a permanent part of Israel's worship.
17: David wishes to build a temple. God promises instead to build David a lasting house and throne. David prays in wonder.
The promise looks ahead to the Messiah.
18: David defeats the surrounding nations and dedicates the plunder to the Lord.
He rules with justice for all his people.
19: David's envoys are shamed, and Joab defeats the Ammonites and their Syrian allies.
"Be strong, and let the Lord do what seems good to him."
20: The Ammonite capital falls, and David's men kill Philistine giants.
The Chronicler passes over David's sin with Bathsheba; his interest is the Temple.
21: David counts Israel out of pride. A plague follows. He buys Ornan's threshing floor at full price and offers sacrifice, and fire falls from heaven.
This is the site where the Temple will stand.
22: David gathers stone, iron, cedar and gold, and charges Solomon to build. He himself has shed too much blood to do it.
David prepares a work he will not live to see finished.
23: David counts the Levites and assigns them to assist the priests and to thank and praise God morning and evening.
Worship needs many kinds of service.
24: The priests are arranged by lot into twenty-four groups to serve in turn.
Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, belonged to one of these divisions.
25: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun and their sons are set apart to make music in the Lord's house.
Sacred music is a real ministry.
26: Levites are assigned to guard the gates and look after the treasuries.
Humble tasks keep God's house in order.
27: Twelve army divisions serve a month each. Tribal leaders and stewards of the king's property are named.
28: Before the assembly David gives Solomon the plans for the Temple and tells him to serve God with a whole heart.
"Be strong and do it. The Lord God is with you."
29: David and the leaders give generously. David prays, "All things come from you, and of your own have we given you." Solomon is made king, and David dies.
Everything we offer God was his gift first.
